Vulnerability: The isolated demonstration concatenates SQL; the normal route uses bound parameters.
Countermeasure: Parameterized search and publication filtering; synthetic exploit comparison and regression tests pass.

Vulnerability: Omitting per-record authorization would expose another user record; current predicates reject that access.
Countermeasure: Owner-or-staff predicates on records; default denial; cross-user tests pass. Collaborator grants are not implemented.

Threat Agent: Human error or failure - Deployment administrator
Vulnerability: Temporary pg_dump copies are not encrypted by the application; a local user able to read them can recover records.
Countermeasure: Temporary-directory cleanup and controlled operator access; application backup encryption and custody evidence remain proposed.

Threat Agent: Human error or failure - Developer mistake then external attacker
Vulnerability: Accidental committed credentials can be copied from Git history; hooks can be bypassed, so CI is independently required.
Countermeasure: Pre-commit rejection, Gitleaks CI and protected branches; rotate any real leaked credential. Native private-repo push protection unavailable.

Threat Agent: Espionage or trespass - Authenticated peer exploiting another query flaw
Vulnerability: Runtime role can select multiple users rows; application predicates are the isolation boundary and a future missed query could bypass it.
Countermeasure: Non-owner runtime and tested application predicates; RLS not implemented.

Threat Agent: Espionage or trespass - Network observer or session thief
Vulnerability: Local HTTP carries bearer credentials without TLS; deployment on an untrusted network would expose them.
Countermeasure: Hashed expiring bearer sessions and revocation; local HTTP only. Production HTTPS remains required. No cookie authentication.

Vulnerability: Backup exercise has no independent immutable recovery generation; compromise of the same operator host may destroy both data and reachable copies.
Countermeasure: Verified local restore is a prerequisite, not offsite resilience. Proposed immutable independent recovery, segregated credentials and rehearsed incident recovery.

Threat Agent: Information extortion - Ransomware operator with credentials or DB exploit
Vulnerability: A stolen administrator credential can alter research data; runtime restriction does not constrain the separately privileged setup identity.
Countermeasure: Separate non-owner runtime, loopback DB and tested restore; protect setup credentials and add independent immutable backups before production.

Vulnerability: Without bounds, search and graph processing can exhaust resources; current route caps and worker lifecycle limits mitigate that case.
Countermeasure: Rate/body limits; staff-only solver; 5000 steps, 25000 edges, 50000 memberships, 2 MiB body; two Python workers, five-second timeout, 8 MiB output ceiling. No OS memory sandbox.

Threat Agent: Sabotage or vandalism - Compromised or faulty worker process
Vulnerability: Status-only worker validation accepted incomplete SUCCESS objects before correction.
Countermeasure: Full structural/type/membership validation; malformed object yields WORKER_PROTOCOL/502; worker process is bounded.

Threat Agent: Sabotage or vandalism - Malicious database administrator
Vulnerability: Runtime audit grants prevent modification, but the database owner can still alter or delete audit events.
Countermeasure: Runtime INSERT/SELECT-only audit grants tested; external tamper-resistant audit storage and administrator oversight remain proposed.
